title: Ending the Session for Form
story: The coach stopped the track session when Tomas's stride shortened, though the watch still showed time left on the plan. Teammates wanted the last repeats, because a public chart recorded only work that was finished. Tomas said he could complete the set. The coach pointed to his changing form, not to the clock. Repeats run with a collapsing stride would train him to accept a poor pattern, and the chart would call that success. They logged the session as cut short for form, and the repeats moved to the next morning, when he was fresh. A finished list, the coach said, was a poor guide to recovery.

vocabulary.definition: The length and shape of a running step
Set pieces of the session done again
A public record of completed work
A way of moving that can become a habit
Getting back to a state ready for good work

quiz.question: What change brought the session to a stop?
options: Tomas's running stride grew shorter
The watch battery went dead
The public chart was switched off
A teammate walked off the track
quiz.explanation: The coach stopped the session when Tomas's stride shortened.
quiz.supportingSentence: The coach stopped the track session when Tomas's stride shortened, though the watch still showed time left on the plan.

quiz.question: When were the unfinished repeats given a new slot?
options: The next morning, once he was fresh
That same evening, after a team vote
A weekend race in another town
The opening minute of the same session
quiz.correctAnswer: The next morning, once he was fresh
quiz.explanation: The repeats moved to the next morning, when he was fresh.
quiz.supportingSentence: They logged the session as cut short for form, and the repeats moved to the next morning, when he was fresh.

quiz.question: Why is a completed set still a poor result here?
options: Bad form would be trained and then recorded as success
The watch was set up for a different sport
Another club had booked the track
Tomas had already raced that morning
quiz.correctAnswer: Bad form would be trained and then recorded as success
quiz.explanation: Finishing with a collapsing stride would teach a poor pattern and still look complete on the chart.
quiz.supportingSentence: Repeats run with a collapsing stride would train him to accept a poor pattern, and the chart would call that success.

quiz.question: What does recovery mean in the coach's last remark?
options: Becoming ready to train well again
A public list of finished repeats
The last lap saved on the watch
A vote taken by teammates
quiz.correctAnswer: Becoming ready to train well again
quiz.explanation: Recovery means getting ready for sound training, which a finished list does not measure.
quiz.supportingSentence: A finished list, the coach said, was a poor guide to recovery.

quiz.question: Why mention a chart that counts only finished work?
options: To show the pressure that makes an early stop look like failure
To announce that the chart was abolished
To name the maker of the watch
To prove Tomas was the fastest runner
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the pressure that makes an early stop look like failure
quiz.explanation: The chart explains why teammates treat a stopped session as a failure.
quiz.supportingSentence: Teammates wanted the last repeats, because a public chart recorded only work that was finished.
